claims.text: The baseline material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Baseline HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
Baseline HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of about 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Baseline HfMoTaTiZr has a density of about 10.21 g/cm³.
Additive manufacturing can introduce a controlled, uniformly distributed 10–15% open-lattice porosity into HfMoTaTiZr.
A 10–15% open-lattice porosity will reduce bulk density by approximately 10–15%.
Porous HfMoTaTiZr will retain at least 1440 MPa yield strength at 25 °C.
Porous HfMoTaTiZr will retain at least 770 MPa yield strength at 1000 °C.
HfMoTaTiZr has a BCC/B2 matrix in which load-bearing columns and subgrain features can be preserved.
Strategically removing material from regions of low stress demand reduces overall density.
Dense load-bearing columns will preserve the alloy's capacity to carry stress despite porosity.
Columnar subgrain structures preserve dislocation storage.
Preserved dislocation storage and confined deformation will limit the porosity-induced loss of yield strength.
Keeping porosity at or below 15% and uniformly distributed will avoid excessive stress concentrations and premature failure.
Oxidation within pores or microstructural inhomogeneity may reduce fatigue life or toughness.
Mechanical comparisons will use tensile tests at 25 °C and 1000 °C at approximately 10^-3 s^-1.
The experiment includes 0%, 5%, 10%, and 15% prescribed-porosity groups, with the 0% group serving as the control.
The hypothesis is rejected if a 10–15% porosity sample fails either strength-retention threshold or achieves less than a 10% density reduction.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly described as as-cast, but the intervention and experiment fabricate it by laser additive manufacturing. An additively manufactured specimen is not itself as-cast unless the lattice is introduced into a separately cast precursor, which is not specified.
